title: Poseidon — Echoes in later ages
summary: Poseidon rules the sea with his trident and shakes the earth as god of earthquakes. This study traces the myth's afterlife.
body:
Poseidon rules the sea with his trident and shakes the earth as god of earthquakes. He contested Athena for patronage of Athens and lost.

Long after its gods lost worshippers, Poseidon kept working — in Renaissance painting, in Romantic poetry, in modern film. Each age found its own anxieties reflected in the old story. Viewed through a narrative lens, Poseidon is examined as story — its plot, its pacing, and the moments that make it unforgettable.

Myths survive by being reusable. Poseidon proved endlessly reusable. A third sub-question asks how Poseidon was visualized — in vase painting, sculpture, or temple relief. Related entries in this archive: Dionysus and Bhagavad Gita.
key_points: Afterlife of Poseidon through the centuries.
